page.seoTitle: React Coding Interview Questions with Solutions
page.description: The components and hooks that come up in React machine coding rounds — debounced search, custom hooks, modals, infinite scroll, autocomplete — with worked solutions.

intro.text: The machine coding round is usually 30 to 45 minutes to build one small component. Nobody expects a finished product. What is being marked is whether you clarify the requirements before typing, choose sensible state, handle the empty, loading and error cases, and clean up after yourself.

Two habits earn marks in every one of these: say what you are about to do before you do it, and mention the edge case even if you decide not to implement it. Each solution below notes what the interviewer is actually watching for.

questions.question: Build a counter with increment, decrement and reset
questions.shortAnswer: One piece of state and three handlers. Use the functional updater form, and keep the initial value in a constant so reset has something to return to.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: The functional updater instead of `setCount(count + 1)`, disabling the buttons at the bounds rather than silently clamping, and using a real `<button>` so it is keyboard accessible. It takes two minutes; spend the rest asking whether bounds or a step size are wanted.

followUps: What if two increments happen in the same tick?

questions.question: Build a search input that debounces its API call
questions.shortAnswer: Keep the input controlled for instant feedback, debounce the value with a custom hook, and fire the request from an effect keyed on the debounced value with cancellation in the cleanup.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: Cancelling the previous request so a slow early response cannot overwrite a fast later one, skipping the empty query, and clearing the timeout on cleanup. Mentioning that TanStack Query would give you all of this plus caching shows you know where the line between exercise and production is.

followUps: What happens if the user clears the input mid-request?
Where would a loading state go?

questions.question: Build a todo list with add, toggle and delete
questions.shortAnswer: One array of objects in state, updated immutably. Give each item a real id rather than using the index, and use a form so Enter submits.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: Immutable updates, stable ids, trimming and rejecting empty input, a `form` so the keyboard works, and an empty state. Candidates who use the array index as the key and mutate with `push` lose the round here, not later.

followUps: How would you add a filter for completed items?

questions.question: Write a custom useFetch hook
questions.shortAnswer: Hold data, error and status in one state object, fetch in an effect keyed on the URL, abort in the cleanup, and return the triple. Say out loud that in production you would use a query library.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: Checking `response.ok`, because `fetch` does not reject on a 404; ignoring `AbortError` so a cancelled request is not shown as a failure; one state object instead of three `useState` calls that can disagree; and noticing that an inline `options` object would restart the effect on every render.

followUps: Why is `options` not in the dependency array?

questions.question: Implement a usePrevious hook
questions.shortAnswer: Store the value in a ref and update it in an effect. Because effects run after render, the ref still holds the previous render's value while the component renders.

answer.text: The whole point is the timing: the render reads `ref.current` before the effect overwrites it, so it sees the old value. On the first render it is `undefined`, which callers must handle.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: Whether you can explain **why** it works rather than reciting it. A follow-up is often "what if you need the previous value during render, not after?", where the answer is to store the previous value in state alongside the current one.

followUps: Why a ref rather than state?

questions.question: Build an accordion where only one section is open at a time
questions.shortAnswer: Hold the id of the open section in state rather than a boolean per section, so exclusivity is structural. Toggle to null when the open one is clicked again.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: Making the invalid state unrepresentable: with one `openId` two panels cannot both be open, whereas an array of booleans lets that bug exist. The `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` pair is the detail that separates candidates.

followUps: How would you allow multiple open sections?

questions.question: Build a star rating component
questions.shortAnswer: Render a radio group styled as stars, track the committed value in state and the hovered value separately, and display the hovered value when there is one. Radios give you keyboard support for free.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: Two separate pieces of state for hover and selection, resetting hover on mouse leave, and reaching for radio inputs instead of clickable spans. Almost everyone builds this with `div`s and then cannot answer "how does a keyboard user set a rating?".

followUps: How would you support half stars?

questions.question: Build a pagination component
questions.shortAnswer: Take the current page, total pages and a change handler as props, keep the page in the URL rather than in local state, and render a window of page numbers with ellipses rather than every page.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: Disabling rather than hiding the edge buttons, the ellipsis logic, `aria-current='page'`, and saying that the page number belongs in the query string so the view is shareable and the back button works.

followUps: Why keep the page in the URL?

questions.question: Implement infinite scroll
questions.shortAnswer: Put a sentinel element after the list and observe it with IntersectionObserver. When it becomes visible and you are not already loading, fetch the next page. Disconnect the observer in the effect cleanup.

items: `rootMargin` starts the fetch before the sentinel is actually visible, so the list rarely appears to stall.
The `enabled` flag is how you stop firing while a request is in flight or when there are no more pages.
The ref holding the latest callback keeps the observer from being torn down and recreated on every render.
For very long lists, combine it with virtualisation, or the DOM grows without limit.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: Disconnecting the observer, guarding against duplicate loads, and knowing why a scroll listener is the worse answer. Mentioning that infinite scroll makes the footer unreachable and breaks the back button is a bonus.

followUps: Why not use a scroll event listener?

questions.question: Build an accessible modal dialog
questions.shortAnswer: Render it through a portal, close on Escape and on backdrop click, trap focus inside while it is open, and return focus to the element that opened it on close.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: Restoring focus on close, locking body scroll and undoing it in the cleanup, stopping the click inside from reaching the backdrop handler, and knowing that a full focus trap needs Tab to cycle. Saying "in production I would use the native `<dialog>` element or a headless library" is a correct and welcome answer.

followUps: How would you implement the Tab cycle?
What does the native `<dialog>` element give you for free?

questions.question: Build an autocomplete with keyboard navigation
questions.shortAnswer: Debounce the query, keep the suggestion list and a highlighted index in state, and handle ArrowUp, ArrowDown, Enter and Escape on the input. Wire up the combobox ARIA attributes so the highlighted option is announced.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: Wrapping the index rather than clamping it, `preventDefault` on the arrow keys so the caret does not jump, `onMouseDown` instead of `onClick` so the selection happens before the input blurs, and resetting the highlight when the results change. This is a 45 minute exercise: agree on scope first.

followUps: How would you handle a slow response arriving after a newer one?

questions.question: Implement a useLocalStorage hook
questions.shortAnswer: Wrap useState, read the stored value lazily on first render, write on change, and guard every access with try/catch because storage can be unavailable or hold invalid JSON.

answer.title: What is being marked
answer.text: The lazy initialiser so storage is read once rather than on every render, the try/catch around both operations, and noticing the server rendering problem: `window` does not exist during SSR, so the read has to move into an effect if the app is server rendered.

followUps: How would you make this work with server rendering?
How would you keep two tabs in sync?
